text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 22 in history.
1797 - The first parachute jump was made by Frenchman Andre-Jacques Garnerin from a balloon 680 metres (2,230 feet) above the Parc Monceau in Paris.
1811 - Franz Liszt born. Hungarian composer and legendary piano virtuoso, he composed some notably difficult music for the piano and was the originator of the modern piano recital.
1844 - Sarah Bernhardt (Henriette Rosine Bernard) born. French actress known as "The Divine Sarah". Renowned for her portrayals of tragic heroines.
1887 - John Reed born. U.S. journalist who covered the Bolshevik Revolution in Russia which he described in "Ten Days That Shook the World".

1906 - French Post-Impressionist painter Paul Cezanne died. His work influenced many 20th century artists. Among his best known works are "Card Players" and "Mont Sainte-Victoire with Large Pine Trees".

1909 - French aviator Elise de Laroche, better known by her self-assumed title Baronne de Laroche, made her first solo flight -- a distance of 300 metres (yards). In March 1910, she became the first qualified woman pilot.

1943 - Catherine Deneuve born. French actress who played leads in both French and international films. Long described as one of the world's most beautiful women, she was named goodwill ambassador to UNESCO in 1994.

1962 - President John Kennedy announced that a Soviet missile base was being built in Cuba and ordered a U.S. naval blockade of ships carrying equipment there. The blockade came into effect two days later.
1964 - French writer Jean-Paul Sartre rejected the Nobel Prize for Literature saying it would reduce the impact of his writing.
1973 - Catalan cellist Pablo Casals died. One of the great cellists, he did much to bring Bach into the standard repertory.
